1. Allowed, subject to all just exceptions.

2. This petition has been filed under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 (in short,
'Cr.P.C.') seeking quashing of FIR No.179/2022 registered at Police Station: Geeta Colony,
Shahadara District, Delhi, under Sections 498A/406/34 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 (in short,
'IPC'), along with all other proceedings arising therefrom, on the basis of a settlement.

sentences.text: Pursuant to the above settlement, the petitioner no.1 and the respondent no.2 have been granted a decree of divorce vide order dated 06.10.2023 by the learned Family Court.

7. The respondent no.2 who is personally present in Court and has been duly identified by the Investigating Officer (IO), reaffirms the abovementioned settlement and states that she has settled all the disputes with the petitioners out of her own free will and without any coercion.
The respondent no.2 submits that she has no objection if the present FIR is quashed.
8. The petitioners have given a Demand Draft of Rs.50,000/- to the respondent no.2 in Court.
9. I have perused the contents of the FIR and also the settlement between the parties.

10. Keeping in view the fact that the disputes between the parties arose out of a matrimonial relationship, and now the same have been amicably settled, a decree of divorce has also been granted to the petitioner no.1 and respondent no.2 pursuant to the settlement, and also looking into the nature of the allegations made in the complaint, in my opinion, no useful purpose would be served in keeping the FIR alive.
In fact, it would rather create further acrimony between the parties and will be an unnecessary burden on the State exchequer.
